recipes.name: Broccoli and Cauliflower Casserole
ingredients_raw: 1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of chicken soup

steps.text: In a saucepan bring water to a boil. Add rice and stir. Reduce heat, cover and simmer for 20 minutes. Drain and set aside.
Simmer broccoli and cauliflower florets in water for 10 minutes, or until crunchy. Meanwhile, preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

In a large saucepan, melt butter and saute onion. Stir cauliflower, broccoli and rice into the saucepan. Once the vegetables and rice are coated, stir in the cheese, chicken soup and milk. Transfer the entire mixture to a 9x13 inch baking dish and sprinkle the crackers on top.
Bake in a preheated 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) oven for 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Broccoli and Cauliflower Casserole
raw_recipe.description: This is a favorite family recipe that I ate quite a bit of when I was pregnant. It’s just one of those things that you can’t get enough of!

review.reviewBody: This is awesome, simple and easy to make a little more healthy. I didn't tweek it much. Just added 2 cloves garlic, low sodium/fat soups, no salt cracker, cut the butter down to 1/4 cup. I also increased the rice to 1 cup and mixed the soups with the milk before I poured over the ingredients. This fits perfectly in the rectangle pampered chef stone. Someone mentioned that they wouldn't add the crackers next time because the next day they were soggy; however, my family liked the flavour of the cracker in the leftovers - tasted like a buttery stuffing. I also have a kitchen scale so i converted to help you out (cause I didnt know how much was 10 oz of broccoli or cauliflower) 10 oz broccloli florets is about 4cups, 10 oz. cauliflower florets is about 3 cups. This of course depends on how you chop, but at least it can give you an idea.

I made this without the rice and used fresh broccoli and cauliflower. I increased the quantity of broccoli & cauliflower to 11 oz. each (using a kitchen scale), and pre-cooked the veggies with the sauteed onion for about 10 min with 1/4 cup of water in my large covered frying pan. Then I added the soup, milk and cubed Velveeta, and cooked covered on low heat until the cheese melted. Then I put into a 9X13 glass baking dish at 300 degrees F for 1 hour, because we had appetizers at a neighbor's house. I also omitted the crushed cracker topping. It turned out beautifully. Wish I had taken a picture.

Loved this!! Followed the proportions exactly but made a few subs: swapped 3 oz of cauliflower for diced carrots; used Monterey jack, havarti and sharp cheddar; cream of mushroom, plant based butter, oat milk and added 2-3 cloves garlic, minced (sautéed half with onion, added the other half to the mix before baking.) Lightly steamed veggies instead of simmering as someone else recommended. So delicious!!

Trying this my way :) Using up fresh cauliflower, broccoli and carrots today at my house. Steamed them after cleaning and cutting into bit sized pieces. Kept them separate so steaming was accurate. Had about 4 c each broccoli and cauliflower cooked and about 2 c cooked carrots. Divided veg between three casseroles (one bigger than the others). In each I put one third of each type of veggie. Don't use canned soup so I made 5 c medium cream sauce with olive oil, butter, flour and veg broth (homemade), add sauteed onions, garlic thyme, parsley, sage and rosemary. In whatever amount suits your taste. add at least 1 cup of sauce to each casserole and mix(big one will take at least two c). First batch will get buttered crumbs when it gets used/cooked off on Wednesday night dinner with pork chops and tossed salad. The second casserole will get white sauce & sautéed fresh mushrooms and will be topped with crumbled bacon. This will be the main dish on Thursday with lemon-butter asparagus and fresh fruit. And lastly the bigger dish will get at least two c white sauce 1 cup cooked rice, sautéed chicken, cheese and sauteed fresh mushrooms for Sunday dinner per the recipe above. So using the basic premise to make three dishes out of a lot of veggies. Also makes cooking easier in the week. Smells great so far looking forward to the results:)Thanks!

I liked this recipe, though I changed a *bunch* of stuff for my preferences. First, I used frozen cauliflower and broccoli, which I steamed for almost 10 minutes before adding to the casserole. Next time I will use fresh veggies and steam them a little longer because the texture was kind of tough. I omitted the onions because I just don't like them, so there was no need for the butter. I substituted 1-2 cups of shredded carrots for the rice to increase the veggie content and that worked (plus it added a nice pop of color). I used cream of mushroom soup because I had it on hand and about 2/3 a pound of extra sharp cheddar cheese. I melted the cheese with the soup and milk before adding the veggies since the cheddar cubes needed a little more time to integrate into the sauce. After baking for 30 minutes the flavor was good, but the sauce was runny and the veggies were still too crisp. So I baked it for another hour in 20 minute increments. It ended up being ok that night, but the next day it was awesome. The leftover factor took it from 3 stars to 4. If I can work out the kinks (thicken the sauce, soften the veggies), I might get mine up to 5 star status.

Saute minced garlic with half onion in 2 tbsp butter then add cooked rice/cauliflower mixture with 1 can of cream of mushroom and 1 cup of milk in pan. Stir until smooth. Pour mixture in casserole dish and toss with half mozzarella and half cheddar cheese mixture . Top with breadcrumbs. Bake approx. 30 min. A definite crowd pleaser. Arborio rice worked great but make sure you boil it al dente. Do not overcook.

Yes, we made this as a side to Christmas dinner we really enjoyed it! I made quite a few changes but they all worked well. I used 2 cups fresh brocc & 2c fresh cauliflour and par boiled both for 10 mins..I used 1 can cream of mushroom soup and 2 cups mild cheddar...1/2 cup white rice and 1/2 cup long brown rice...1/2 cup finely chopped raw celery..only used 1/2 cube of butter thought a whole cube would be too much...it fit perfectly in a square 8 x 8 baking pan and we stuck little pieces of raw broccoli and cauliflour down into the casserole to give it a crunch..this came out great...will def make it again! Nice because you can modify it so much! Oh also we put those French's french fried onions on the top instead of crackers..worked good! We cooked it for about 45 mins on 350 until just brown. Thanks for this nice recipe!

I wasn't really sure how to rate this. I hate it when people change a recipe and then rate it and I'm sure that made as stated it would be delicious. However, due to health issues, I cut the butter to 1/4 cup and the pound of "processed" cheese to a half pound of shredded cheddar and used reduced fat/sodium mushroom soup. I also upped the milk to a soup can as it seemed a little dry, I suppose due to less butter and cheese. It was delicious. I topped with a mixture of seasoned bread crumbs and grated Parmesan to cut the carbs and some of the salt. The next time I'll try it with some cubed ham or left over rotisserie chicken as a main dish casserole.

Very tasty! I made substitutions to the recipe to include ingredients that were on hand. I used Chedder and Pepper Jack cheeses, cream of mushroom soup (reduced fat/sodium), and I added one cup of cooked Kamut (ancient Egyptian grain). I lightly steamed the veggies to ensure some texture and nutrients.

I didn't have all ingredients, so substituted shredded cheddar, mozzarella and Monterey cheese, I use jasmine rice, no ritz crackers so I used stove stop, chicken flavor stuffing for topping, Delish! (I added 1 jalapeño pepper & oregano to onion sauté, salt, pepper & garlic to taste).
Very simple and definitely a dish that would be great for the Holidays!

I began by sauteing a medium red onion, Portobello mushrooms, and minced garlic in Extra Virgin olive oil then adding broccoli and cauliflower florets to the pan while at the same time boiling water for my brown rice. For the soup mixture, I combined by whisking 2 cans of Cream of Chicken soup, 1/2 cup of Parmesan cheese, 5 oz. of whole milk, and a tbsp of chopped fresh basil. To assemble the casserole, I placed the cooked brown rice in a 9x13 glass baking dish along with a finely chopped bunch of scallions and then mixed in my veggies from the pan. Next, I folded in my soup mixture and 8 oz. of grated Extra Sharp Cheddar cheese. Before placing in the 350 degrees F. oven, I topped everything off with a generous layer of Italian style bread crumbs to form a nice and savory crust. Woooooo Buddy, I gotta say, this was Delicious with a capital "D." Served with a spicy coated chicken breast and boiled egg slices, this was a fantastic meal which earned me the prized golden Stamp of Approval (SOA) from Mi Gato Loco.
I made this and my husband and I loved it. I used sharp cheddar cheese instead of processed cheese. I also cooked up some ground turkey and added it to make a meal out of a side dish.
Don’t forget to season with salt and pepper or maybe some garlic. Husband loved it
Used cheddar cheese. Otherwise recipe as shown. Very good. Added smoked sausage slices the next night for leftover meal.
I substituted a few things.....I used cashew cheese,almond milk,vegan cream cheese,vegan mayo and vegan sour cream...... Very tasty........I also used gluten free buttery crackers on top.....
Delicious.....my kids loved it.

I really like this recipe and so do the rest of my family! I even managed to make it twice in a week xD. I added some carrots too and cut the crackers in favor of another cheese layer, cut back on the butter a bit and actually used cream of mushroom soup instead of chicken. What a wonderful dish!
Good, went with mushroom soup, shredded cheddar& bread crumbs. Next time, add ham to make complete meal
Yummy! I will definitely make this again!
This was a great meat free cassarole that is very tasty and easy to make . I would definatly make this again .
